key_insight: VATC combines declared agent traffic, router-side verification, and rate-limited priority scheduling to reduce agent queuing delay while protecting human traffic from spoofed floods.
engineering_relevance: Network engineers could use VATC to prioritize latency-sensitive AI agents, but benefits depend on classifier reliability and careful queue configuration.
method: Mark agent traffic with a reserved DSCP value.
Demote flows that contradict their agent declaration to below best-effort service.
Serve accepted agent traffic through a rate-limited priority queue.
evidence_signal: Across two simulators and Linux-kernel tests, VATC cut mean agent queuing delay 98% versus DiffServ in a constructed burst assuming immediate verification, increased human delay 12%, and kept human latency 11 times below DiffServ under a spoofed flood.
watch_item: Results used synthetic or sandbox-scale traffic; the live classifier missed six agent-pattern spoofers, and emulated network delay erased one timing feature’s ability to distinguish agents from humans.
paper_title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing
